bug_semantics: Scriban expression evaluation (CWE-400) lets a template author exhaust memory or CPU on three paths that ignore existing LoopLimit/LimitToString controls. Vector 1: ScriptBinaryExpression.CalculateToString implements string*int as an unbounded C# for-loop that Appends into a StringBuilder, so '{{ 'AAAA' * 500000000 }}' attempts a multi-gigabyte allocation even when LimitToString defaults to 1MB. Vector 2: CalculateLongWithInt and CalculateBigIntegerNoFit apply BigInteger << (int)right with no cap, so '{{ 1 << 100000000 }}' allocates an arbitrarily large integer (Power is capped with MaxBigInteger, but shift is not). Vector 3: '..' / '..<' produce lazy RangeInclude/RangeExclude iterators; ArrayFunctions.Size fully enumerates via Cast<object>().Count() and Join appends with no size bound, never calling StepLoop(), so '{{ (0..1000000000) | array.size }}' burns CPU despite LoopLimit=1000. OutOfMemoryException typically terminates the host process. Vendor/CVE range is all versions before 7.0.0.
flaw_origin: The public-history root commit 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589 (2016-01-25, 'Initial version') first wrote the unbounded string-multiply loop in CalculateToString, the unbounded RangeInclude/RangeExclude iterators, ArrayFunctions.Size/Join enumeration of IEnumerable, and LoopLimit/StepLoop confined to ScriptForStatement/ScriptWhileStatement. That is the smallest surviving first-write of vectors 1 and 3; the commit has no parent and no finer public member. Vector 2 is a later sibling: 4175ec0cd75adcc459810abbf9e3e0a9d360ffb3 (2020-04-15) added unbounded BigInteger ShiftLeft next to a Power/MaxBigInteger cap that was never applied to shifts; its parent e5fcf501 lacks those shift cases. Subsequent refactors (namespace moves, CalculateToString rewrite from rightText to leftText, BigInteger range overloads) preserved the unbounded mechanisms rather than introducing them. LimitToString (b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95, 2020-05-19) still did not cover string multiplication.

reasoning: CVE-2026-74785 is a live VulnCheck publication of the vendor GHSA-xw6w-9jjh-p9cr issue (not withdrawn/rejected), so this is a real CWE-400, not FALSE_POSITIVE. The three DoS vectors share one expression-evaluation resource-bound gap: C# loops and lazy ranges that never consult LoopLimit/LimitToString. The BIC is the smallest commit that first wrote those vulnerable lines. git log -S / file contents show the unbounded string*int loop, unbounded range iterators, array.size/join enumeration, and for/while-only StepLoop were all present in the unique public root 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589. Immediate parent is absent (verified rev-parse ^ failure); no finer public member exists, so the initial first-write is a valid BIC rather than a discarded squash aggregate. Later commits that touch the same functions are moves/refactors (0c2d3e0a namespace move, 4175ec0c CalculateToString rewrite, BigInteger range overloads) except vector 2, whose first write is 4175ec0c's unbounded ShiftLeft — a human 2020 sibling in the same file, not a substitute BIC, because the vendor affected range starts at version 0 via vectors 1 and 3. Direct parent of 4175ec0c lacks the shift cases. The 2026 patch 2d01bd15 is the first commit that inserts LimitToString/shift/range guards (absent at its parent) and is contained in annotated tag 7.0.0 but not 6.6.0, matching < 7.0.0 / patched 7.0.0. AI judgment uses only the BIC commit object: Alexandre Mutel authored and committed 'Initial version' with no Co-authored-by/Generated-with/bot identity. Copilot trailers on the fix commits are AI-only-on-fix and are ignored for attribution. Therefore NOT_AI.
